key_insight: VideoScout reframes long video understanding as sequential evidence acquisition, using adaptive pacing to decide how quickly to read, what to keep, when to revisit, and when to answer.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical agent design for long-horizon multimodal systems by expanding usable context coverage without requiring larger visual windows.
method: Multi-turn agent that controls viewing pace over the temporal axis
Two-stage training: supervised cold-start formatting, then trajectory-level RL with DAPO
Composite reward balances answer accuracy, format compliance, and timing alignment via IoU
evidence_signal: The paper reports training on VideoScout-66K, built from over 66K exploration turns and 10K answer-verified trajectories, and evaluates a 7B model on long-video understanding and reasoning benchmarks.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of timing-alignment rewards and trajectory labels, so weak teacher timing or noisy exploration traces could limit robustness.
paper_title: VideoScout: Learning Agentic Active Exploration with Adaptive Reasoning Pacing for Long Video Understanding
